title: 第九章 私塾窗下
content_zh:
次日一早，江砚揣着那方豁角的旧砚台，徒步去了镇上。

    沈家村往东十里，有个不大的集镇，叫青石镇，是这一带乡民赶集、买卖的去处。镇上有间私塾，原主的爹江守文，早年就在那儿给坐馆的先生当过帮工。

    江砚去镇上，是揣着两个心思的。

    明面上的：那笔债，他得想个法子。三贯钱五石粮，他凑不齐，可万一……万一能寻个识字的活计，先挣个一星半点，或是把这方旧砚台、那截秃笔当了换几个钱——哪怕只是个零头，能让他在沈贵面前多争两天工夫，也是好的。

    藏在心底的：他想去那私塾门口看看。原主的爹是在那儿沾上的“识字”，他总觉得，那地方，或许藏着点别的他还不知道的东西。

    镇子比村里热闹些，可也热闹得有限。街上店铺开着的不过半数，行人脚步匆匆，脸上没几分活气。墙根下蹲着衣衫褴褛的流民，伸着冻裂的手，向过路人讨一口吃的。一队挎着腰刀的兵卒从街口大摇大摆地走过,沿街的小贩纷纷低头，往他们脚边的篮子里塞两个铜板、一把干果，赔着笑——分明是变着法子的盘剥。

    江砚冷眼看着，没作声。

    他先去了当铺。可那截秃笔、豁角的旧砚，掌柜的瞧都懒得多瞧一眼，嫌晦气，挥手就把他撵了出来。他又转到几家铺子，想问问要不要写字记账的帮手，人家一听他是沈家村来的、连个保人都没有的孤儿,立刻警惕起来，连连摆手。

    跑了一上午，分文未得。

    江砚也不气馁——他本就没指望一趟就成。揣着砚台，他踱到了镇子东头的那间私塾。

    私塾是一处旧院落，门口挂着块褪色的“明理学塾”木匾。这会儿正是授课的时辰，里头隐隐传出孩童齐声背书的声音。

    江砚没敢进去，只在墙外那扇半开的窗下，悄悄站住了脚。

    他听着里头那位先生抑扬顿挫地讲书，心里头说不出是什么滋味。同样是十几岁的年纪，墙里墙外，竟是两个天差地别的世道。

    讲了一阵书，约莫是课间歇晌，里头的读书声停了。江砚正要走，却听见窗内,那位塾师和一个像是来访的老友，压低了声音闲谈起来。

    “……你是没瞧见那排场。”一个声音感慨道，“城里卫家上月办寿，光是流水席就摆了三天。这世道，饿殍遍野，人家倒是越发的烈火烹油。”

    “卫家么……”塾师叹了口气，“如今这云中城，谁不知道是卫家的天下。听说连城里的驻军，都得看卫家的脸色。”

    江砚的脚步顿住了。

    卫家。
content_en:
Early the next morning, Jiang Yan walked to the town carrying the old inkstone with a square corner.

    Ten miles east of Shenjia Village, there is a small market town called Qingshi Town, which is where the villagers in this area go to market and do business. There is a private school in the town, and the original owner's father, Jiang Shouwen, worked there as a helper for the teacher who was sitting in the school in his early years.

    Jiang Yan went to town with two thoughts in mind.

    On the bright side: He has to find a way to deal with that debt. He couldn't get three guans of money and five shi of grain together, but if... if he could find a job to read, he could earn a little bit first, or he could exchange this old inkstone and that bald pen for a few bucks - even if it was just a small change, it would be good for him to compete with Shen Gui for two more days.

    Hidden deep in his heart: He wanted to go to the door of the private school and have a look. The original owner's father acquired "literacy" there, and he always felt that there might be something else hidden in that place that he didn't know yet.

    The town is more lively than the village, but the liveliness is limited. Only half of the shops on the street were open, and pedestrians walked in a hurry, with little vitality on their faces. Under the wall squatted refugees in ragged clothes, stretching out their frozen hands to beg for a bite of food from passers-by. A group of soldiers armed with swords swaggered through the street. The vendors along the street lowered their heads, stuffed two copper coins and a handful of dried fruits into the baskets at their feet, and smiled - it was obviously a different kind of exploitation.

    Jiang Yan watched coldly and said nothing.

    He went to the pawn shop first. But the shopkeeper didn't bother to take a second look at the old inkstone with a bald pen and a chipped corner. He thought it was unlucky, so he waved his hand and drove him out. He went to several shops to ask if they wanted help with writing and accounting. When people heard that he was an orphan from Shenjia Village who didn't even have a guarantor, they immediately became wary and waved their hands.

    I ran all morning and didn't get a penny.

    Jiang Yan wasn't discouraged - he didn't expect it to happen in one trip. Carrying the inkstone, he walked to the private school at the east end of the town.

    The private school is in an old courtyard, with a faded wooden plaque reading "Ming Li School" hanging at the door. It was the time for teaching, and there was a faint sound of children endorsing books in unison.

    Jiang Yan did not dare to go in, but quietly stood still under the half-open window outside the wall.

    He listened to the gentleman inside speaking in a measured tone, and he couldn't tell what he felt in his heart. They were still in their teens, but inside and outside the wall, there were two completely different worlds.

    After talking for a while, probably during the break, the sound of reading inside stopped. Jiang Yan was about to leave when he heard the private school teacher and an old friend who seemed to be visiting chatting in lowered voices through the window.

    "...You didn't see the splendid scene." A voice said with emotion, "The Wei family in the city held a birthday party last month, and the flowing water banquet was laid out for three days. In this world, people are dying of hunger all over the place, but people are cooking with more and more fire."

    "The Wei family..." The tutor sighed, "Nowadays in Yunzhong City, who doesn't know that the world belongs to the Wei family? I heard that even the garrison in the city has to look at the Wei family's face."

    Jiang Yan's footsteps paused.

    Wei family.
title_en: Chapter 9 Under the private school window
